questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Your mirrors show you everything around you.
Check your mirrors and turn your head to look for blind spots.
Signal and move to the right or left immediately.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and turn your head to look for blind spots.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any vehicle. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes, even after checking your mirrors.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: It connects the front and rear brakes when you use the rear brake.
It automatically knows when to brake based on your riding style.
It applies the brake when you downshift the gears.

questions.correctAnswerText: It connects the front and rear brakes when you use the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Some motorcycles have integrated braking systems. When you apply the rear brake, it links the front and rear brakes together. Check your owner's manual to learn about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Divided roadway ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They warn you about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that a divided roadway is ahead.

questions.question: A motorcycle's horn is ________ a car's horn.
questions.correctAnswerText: Quieter than
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's horn is not as loud as a car's horn. Use your horn when needed, but do not rely on it to stay safe.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, a motorcycle rider has an advantage because:

options.text: A motorcycle accelerates faster than a car.
The rider can stay in the left part of the lane to avoid doors and people on the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: The rider can stay in the left part of the lane to avoid doors and people on the right.
questions.explanation: When passing parked cars on your right, ride in the left part of your lane. This helps you avoid opening doors, people getting out, or people stepping between cars. Only do this if there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign is ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They warn you about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that a stop sign is coming up.

questions.question: How are convex mirrors different from regular mirrors?

options.text: They show a narrower view of the road.
They show a wider view of the road.
They show a clearer view of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They show a wider view of the road.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors on motorcycles show a wider view than flat mirrors. However, they can make vehicles appear farther away than they really are.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Right lane ends
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They warn you about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that the right lane is ending.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, what is the minimum following distance for a motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds
questions.explanation: Keep at least a two-second distance between you and the vehicle ahead under normal conditions. When conditions are bad, use a larger distance.

questions.question: What is one of the best ways to help others see your motorcycle?

options.text: Keep your high beam headlight on.
Paint your motorcycle a dark color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your high beam headlight on.
questions.explanation: The best way to help others see your motorcycle is to keep your headlight on. Use your high beam during the day and night whenever it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: A DOT-compliant helmet:

options.text: Lets you see as much to the sides as you need for safe riding.
Can be dangerous for the rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lets you see as much to the sides as you need for safe riding.
questions.explanation: Some people think helmets limit vision, but this is not true. Any DOT-approved helmet lets you see as much as you need for safe riding.

questions.question: If you are riding behind another vehicle at night, how can you tell if there are bumps ahead on the road?

options.text: Listen for the other vehicle scraping the pavement.
Watch the other vehicle's taillights bounce up and down.
Look at the rear bumper of the vehicle ahead to see if it bounces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch the other vehicle's taillights bounce up and down.
questions.explanation: Watch the vehicle ahead to learn about road conditions at night. If its taillights bounce up and down, bumps are ahead on the road.

questions.question: Alcohol reaches the brain ________ being consumed.
questions.correctAnswerText: within minutes of
questions.explanation: Alcohol reaches your brain within minutes of drinking and starts to affect your riding ability right away. Riding under the influence of alcohol is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, it is usually best to:

options.text: Ride on the right side of the lane.
Ride on the edge of the road.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: Pavement is slippery when rain first starts. The rainwater mixes with oil left by cars. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars ahead of you for the best grip.

questions.question: Riding alongside a vehicle in the next lane is:

options.text: Not recommended because you may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
Recommended if you want to travel at the same speed as the other driver.
Acceptable if you want to race the other driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not recommended because you may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding alongside another vehicle is dangerous. You may be in the driver's blind spot. Also, the vehicle blocks your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: Which factor may affect a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?
questions.correctAnswerText: The amount of alcohol consumed
questions.explanation: The main factors that affect blood alcohol content (BAC) are how much alcohol you drank, how fast you drank it, and your body weight.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, your feet should be:

options.text: Pointed with your toes aiming downward.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the footrests for balance.
questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests for balance. Do not point your toes downward, as they may get caught between the road and the footrests.

questions.question: If you are passing parked vehicles on your right and there is no oncoming traffic, you should ride:

options.text: In the left portion of your lane.
In the right portion of your lane.
In the center of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane. This helps you avoid car doors opening and pedestrians stepping out. If there is oncoming traffic, stay in the center of your lane to have more space around you.

questions.question: If possible, do not ride directly next to another vehicle because:

options.text: Another driver may want to use your lane to pass.
You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
You may have access to escape routes.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding alongside another vehicle is dangerous. You may be in the driver's blind spot, and the driver will not see you. The vehicle may also block your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are separated by:
questions.correctAnswerText: White lines.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Solid lines mean you cannot pass. Dashed lines mean you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the road may be slippery when it is wet.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks while you are braking, you should:

options.text: Keep the tire locked up, as it will help you stop more quickly.
Release the front brake and only use the rear brake.
Release the front brake immediately and re-apply it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake immediately and re-apply it.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while braking, release pressure from the front brake right away. Then slowly re-apply the brake with gentle, controlled pressure.

questions.question: Passengers should:

options.text: Hold onto the rider's hips, waist, or belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold onto the rider's hips, waist, or belt.
questions.explanation: Before you start riding, tell your passenger to hold firmly onto your hips, waist, or belt. Your passenger can also use any secure handholds on the motorcycle.

questions.question: Where is the greatest potential for conflict between you and other vehicles?
questions.correctAnswerText: At an intersection
questions.explanation: Intersections are where most conflicts happen between motorcycles and other vehicles.

questions.question: It is illegal to operate a motorcycle with a blood alcohol content (BAC) of:
questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent.
questions.explanation: In California, it is illegal for drivers 21 or older to operate a motorcycle with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. For drivers under 21, any BAC of 0.01 percent or higher is illegal. Even below the legal limit, riding a motorcycle after drinking can be unsafe.
